title: TheraBreath Survey Reveals Americans’ Oral Care Habits
html:
New TheraBreath™-Commissioned YouGov Survey Reveals How Americans Approach Oral Care Habits, Product Recommendations, and Daily Routines.

Most Americans say they have a consistent oral care routine, but new research suggests consistency doesn’t always mean comprehensive care. According to a nationally representative YouGov survey commissioned by TheraBreath™, many consumers are sticking to routines that may overlook important habits for overall oral health. Eighty-three percent of U.S. adults describe their routine as very or somewhat consistent, and 84% report skipping at least one of the oral care habits tested. Flossing is the most commonly skipped behavior at 45%, followed by tongue cleaning at 44%, using mouthrinse at 43%, and brushing before bed at 42%.

The study also shows that dental professionals remain the clear authority Americans trust when choosing oral care products, despite the increase in information sources. Sixty-one percent of U.S. adults identify a dentist or dental hygienist as their most trusted source for oral care product recommendations, compared with just 2% who select social media or influencers.

“What stands out isn’t that people don’t care about their oral health. Most clearly do,” said Xi Chen, senior director of brand marketing for TheraBreath™. “The challenge is translating good intentions into habits that fit real life. Patients are telling us they trust dental professionals to help them make sense of product choices, understand what’s most important, and build routines they can actually maintain over time.”

The findings suggest an opportunity for dental professionals to help patients build on their existing routines with clear, manageable recommendations rather than an overwhelming list of changes.

The survey also found that nearly half of adults (49%) feel self-conscious at least occasionally in social or professional settings because of an oral health concern, such as bad breath, dry mouth, or a visible oral issue. Twenty-one percent have avoided discussing an oral health concern with a dental professional because it felt embarrassing, reinforcing the value of open, nonjudgmental conversations about sensitive oral care concerns.

Trust Drives Consideration. Results Drive Continued Use.

While dental professionals play a leading role in helping patients navigate oral care choices, the survey indicates that product experience becomes especially important once a product is in use. When asked what most influences whether they continue using an oral care product consistently, 40% selected effectiveness or results, compared with 20% who selected cost or value and 18% who selected a dental professional’s recommendation.

Consumers also want to understand what they are using: 76% say transparency about ingredients and formulation is very or somewhat important when selecting oral care products.

Together, the findings point to a straightforward role for dental professionals: use their trusted position to help patients select appropriate products, explain their intended benefits in understandable terms, and recommend routines patients can realistically maintain. Dental professionals can access TheraBreath™ clinical research, educational resources, and product information, and request samples at https://www.hygienesquad.com/therabreath.

Survey Methodology

All figures, unless otherwise stated, are from YouGov Plc. The total sample size was 1,240 adults. Fieldwork was undertaken August 4–5, 2026. The survey was carried out online. Figures have been weighted and are representative of all U.S. adults aged 18 and older.
